title: The Unseen Doctor of Jaffna: A Hospital's Eternal Vigil
description:
Deep within the aging corridors of Jaffna Teaching Hospital, nurses speak of a presence that never truly left. A faint scent of antiseptic, a sudden chill, a whisper in an empty ward… they say it's the spirit of an old colonial doctor, still making his rounds, forever battling a plague from a time long past.

This episode of Ceylon Dread delves into the enduring legend surrounding this dedicated physician, a story passed down among the hospital staff, blending local history with the chilling persistence of a duty unfulfilled.
fiction_note: Based on Sri Lankan folklore and urban legends; characters and specific events are dramatised for storytelling.

scenes.narration: Have you ever felt a cold touch, somewhere impossibly empty? A whisper that isn't a whisper, but a memory of one, clinging to the air? In the old wing of the Jaffna Teaching Hospital, they say such feelings are not your imagination, especially after the kerosene lamps are lit and the shadows grow long, stretching like skeletal fingers across the worn tile floors. It’s where Nurse Amara first felt it, that peculiar, deep chill, even on the hottest Jaffna night when the air hung heavy and still, smelling of rain on hot ground. But inside, in those quiet corridors, there was a different kind of cold. A cold that seemed to hum with an old, forgotten purpose, a restless energy from another time.
visuals: Wide shot: Long, decaying hospital corridor in Jaffna, dim flickering emergency lights casting long shadows, 35mm film grain, 2am, wide angle.
Detail shot: A single, ancient kerosene lamp on a dusty nursing station desk, casting a small pool of yellow light, a white surgical mask draped over its base, shallow depth of field, close focus.

scenes.narration: Amara was new to the night shift, just two months into her posting at the hospital’s oldest section. Her friends had warned her, of course, their voices low and urgent over cups of strong, sweet tea. Whispers, they said, about the 'doctor who never left.' But Amara, young and practical, dismissed it as old women’s tales, stories spun to scare the new recruits. She knew the wards were old, yes. The plaster peeling in forgotten corners, the tiled floors worn smooth and shiny by generations of hurried footsteps. But a ghost? That was a step too far for her pragmatic mind. Not in modern Sri Lanka, not in a place of healing, where science and medicine held sway.
visuals: Wide shot: A young nurse, Amara, seen from behind, walking down a long, dimly lit hospital corridor, the faint glow of emergency lights reflecting on the polished but worn floor. Late night, 50mm lens.
Detail shot: A cracked windowpane in an old hospital ward, showing a sliver of the moon through thick, humid air outside. Cobwebs in the corner of the frame.

scenes.narration: Then came the smell. It wasn’t the usual hospital antiseptic, sharp and clinical, the familiar scent of disinfectant used to scrub away the day’s ailments. This was different, older, almost sweet, like carbolic acid from another era, a scent that carried the weight of decades. It would bloom out of nowhere, in an empty ward, curling around her, then vanish as quickly as it appeared, leaving her to wonder if she'd imagined it. A cold spot would follow, a sudden, inexplicable drop in temperature that made the hairs on her arms stand up, raising goosebumps on her skin. She’d rub her arms, look around, her eyes scanning the deep shadows, but there was never anyone. Just the low hum of the fluorescent tubes, the distant sounds of the city, and the rhythmic chirping of geckos on the high, cracked walls.
visuals: Wide shot: An empty hospital ward with rows of old metal beds, covered in white sheets. A single, very faint, almost imperceptible blue-white mist hovers near one bed. Early morning light, 35mm.
Detail shot: A tarnished brass nameplate on an old wooden ward door, too weathered to read, glinting faintly under a single bare bulb overhead. Dust motes visible in the light.

scenes.narration: One night, while checking on a sleeping patient, a frail old man whose shallow breaths barely stirred the sheets, Amara heard it. A soft, clear 'shhh,' right beside her ear, close enough to feel a faint stir of air against her cheek. A voice, deep and calm, yet utterly disembodied. She spun around, heart hammering against her ribs, a jolt of pure adrenaline shooting through her. Nothing. The patient slept soundly, undisturbed. Later, she confided in Renuka, a senior nurse whose eyes held the wisdom of many years on these night shifts, her face pale under the dim ward lights. Renuka just nodded slowly, a knowing, weary look in her eyes. “Ah, so he’s made his acquaintance with you too, eh, Amara?” she murmured, stirring her lukewarm tea with a spoon, the clink of ceramic against metal sounding unnaturally loud in the quiet breakroom.
visuals: Wide shot: A young nurse, Amara, turning sharply in an empty hospital ward, looking over her shoulder into the shadows. The patient's form is a blur in the foreground. Low light, wide aperture.
Detail shot: Two hands, one young and one older, clasping a chipped ceramic tea cup on a worn wooden table. Steam rises faintly from the cup, illuminated by a nearby lamp.

scenes.narration: Renuka leaned closer, lowering her voice, the comforting smell of strong Ceylon tea filling the air around them. “They say, you see, during the colonial times, there was a terrible plague that swept through Jaffna. Not like the sicknesses we see now. This was swift, merciless. Thousands died, entire families wiped out. This hospital, this very wing where we sit, was overwhelmed. Beds overflowed into the corridors, the morgue couldn't keep up. And there was one doctor, a dedicated, quiet man, Dr. Rajaratnam. He worked day and night, barely sleeping, his face etched with fatigue and sorrow. They say he lost his own family to the sickness, his wife, his young children, but he never stopped. He believed, you see, he could save them all. He had to.” Her voice trailed off, a distant temple drum beginning its rhythmic thrum, a solemn beat against the stillness of the night.
visuals: Wide shot: Two nurses, one older, one younger, seated on a bench in a dimly lit hospital corridor, their backs to the camera. The older nurse is gesturing slightly. Night time, 85mm lens.

Detail shot: A faded, sepia-toned photograph of a stern-looking man in colonial-era surgical attire, pinned to a bulletin board with other notices, half-hidden by shadow. The image is slightly blurred.

scenes.narration: But the plague was too strong, too relentless. Dr. Rajaratnam worked himself to exhaustion, his mind racing through every remedy, every new technique, desperate to find a cure. He pushed past human limits, driven by a profound sense of duty and a grief that consumed him. He died here, in this hospital, some say right in the operating theatre, his body finally giving out from sheer fatigue and despair, still clutching a surgical instrument, as if in mid-operation. And his spirit, they say, never found peace. He’s still here, conducting his eternal rounds, a shadow among the living, trying to save the patients he couldn’t save then. That faint antiseptic smell? It’s his presence. The cold spots? His unending grief, a chill that lingers in the air. Amara listened, a shiver running down her spine, not just from the cold, but from the weight of such sorrow.
visuals: Wide shot: A long, empty surgical ward with old equipment shrouded under white sheets. A faint, almost transparent silhouette of a tall figure in a white coat can be seen at the far end, disappearing around a corner. Low light, slightly desaturated colors.
Detail shot: An old, tarnished surgical clamp lying forgotten on a dusty metal trolley in a corner, catching a sliver of weak moonlight from a high window. The metal gleams faintly.

scenes.narration: A week later, the story felt less like folklore and more like a premonition, a chilling whisper of what was to come. A young boy, barely ten, was brought in with a severe respiratory infection. His small chest heaved with every breath. Amara watched his shallow, struggling breaths, a knot of cold fear tightening in her stomach as his condition worsened rapidly throughout the evening. Outside, a tropical storm raged, a furious symphony of wind and water. Rain lashed against the windows, blurring the world beyond, and the wind howled through the ancient eaves of the hospital, a mournful cry. The power flickered, dipped, then plunged the entire old wing into utter darkness. Only the weak, yellow glow of the emergency lights remained, struggling valiantly against the encroaching gloom.
visuals: Wide shot: A small, frail boy lying in a hospital bed, barely visible in the dim emergency lighting. Amara, a silhouette, stands anxiously beside him. Rain streaks down the outside of the window, creating blurry patterns. 50mm, long exposure.
Detail shot: Raindrops furiously hitting a rusty, grimy hospital window pane, blurring the distant lights of Jaffna. The glass is old, distorted.

scenes.narration: The boy’s breathing grew more laboured, each gasp a desperate struggle. Amara fumbled for the oxygen mask, her hands trembling in the near-darkness, her fingers clumsy with rising panic. The air in the ward grew heavy, thick and still, saturated with that old, familiar antiseptic scent, now more potent than ever before. A distinct, icy chill wrapped around her, colder than any draft, a presence she could almost feel pressing in. Then, she heard it clearly: the soft, precise clinking of metal instruments, a sound impossibly close, yet unseen, like a surgeon preparing for an urgent procedure. A faint, almost imperceptible pressure on her arm, guiding her hand, steadying it, moving it with a deliberate, calm certainty. A whisper, this time urgent, though she couldn't make out the exact words, a sense of quiet command. The boy coughed, a deep, rattling sound that seemed to clear something deep within his chest.
visuals: Wide shot: A nurse, Amara, hunched over a patient in a dark ward, illuminated only by a single, weak emergency lamp on the wall. Shadows dance wildly. A faint, almost transparent hand is hovering near her own. 35mm lens.
Detail shot: A faint, shimmering outline of an old-fashioned stethoscope, half-visible against a dark wall in a hospital corridor, reflecting the weak emergency light. The metal is subtly glowing.

scenes.narration: Just as Amara felt a surge of pure panic, a wave of relief washed over her as the power surged back, flooding the ward with harsh, fluorescent light. Her eyes adjusted, blinking against the sudden brightness. The boy was still breathing, but his colour seemed better, his small chest rising and falling with less strain, his breaths less shallow, more even. On the clean white sheet beside him, near his head, a faint, almost invisible imprint. A very specific, perfectly clean circle, like the base of a small, heavy glass bottle, still slightly damp. And that unique, ancient antiseptic scent was stronger than ever, clinging to the air like a signature. Amara looked around the now brightly lit ward, her gaze darting from corner to corner. Nobody. Nothing out of place. Yet the lingering presence, the undeniable feeling of a duty fulfilled, was palpable.
visuals: Wide shot: A hospital ward suddenly bathed in harsh fluorescent light, revealing the starkness of the old room. Amara stands frozen by the patient's bedside, looking around in disbelief. 24mm lens, stark contrast.
Detail shot: A pristine white hospital sheet on a bed, with a faint, perfect circular wet mark, like the base of a bottle, almost invisible. The texture of the sheet is crisp, slightly wrinkled.

scenes.narration: Later that morning, as the sun began to warm the red earth roads outside, bringing a fresh, clean smell after the storm, Amara recounted the night’s events to Renuka. Her voice was hushed, filled with a blend of awe and disbelief. The senior nurse listened quietly, stirring her morning tea, nodding slowly, her eyes distant, as if seeing something beyond the visible. “He was here, then,” Renuka said, her voice soft, almost a whisper. “Dr. Rajaratnam. He still tries, you see. Even in the darkest hour, when all hope seems lost, he finds a way to help.” Amara couldn’t argue. The boy, against all odds, was stable, improving with remarkable speed. How could she explain it otherwise? The clinking, the cold touch, the precise, guiding pressure on her arm. She had felt a hand, a very real, very present, helping hand.
visuals: Wide shot: Two nurses, Amara and Renuka, standing by a ward window, looking out at a sun-drenched Jaffna landscape with jak trees and red earth roads. Their conversation is quiet, contemplative. Morning light, 50mm.

Detail shot: A faded framed photograph of an old hospital building, possibly from the colonial era, hanging crookedly on a peeling wall, illuminated by a shaft of morning light. Dust motes dance in the air.

scenes.narration: Now, Amara still works the night shifts in the old wing. She still smells the carbolic, feels the occasional chill that passes through the corridors, hears the faint, distant sounds of an unseen doctor’s rounds, a soft tread on the worn tiles. But the fear has lessened, replaced by a strange respect, a quiet understanding that settles deep within her. In the dead of night, when the rest of Jaffna sleeps, the dedicated Dr. Rajaratnam walks these corridors, eternally committed to his patients, his duty unending. And sometimes, she wonders, perhaps he’s not alone in his vigil. Perhaps, in their own way, the living nurses also keep watch, their lamps burning, their footsteps echoing, side by side with the Unseen Doctor, a silent, shared commitment to healing. If you liked this story, do follow for more tales from Ceylon Dread.
visuals: Wide shot: A lone nurse, Amara, walking slowly down a long, empty hospital corridor. The emergency lights cast a faint glow, and a distant, shadowy figure seems to be just turning a corner far ahead. Early morning, blue hour light filtering in.

Detail shot: A single, old-fashioned medical chart, yellowed and worn, lying on a wooden desk. A quill pen rests beside it, catching the faint light from a single overhead bulb. The name 'Dr. Rajaratnam' is faintly visible at the top of the chart, blurred.

visuals: Vertical shot: A long, dark hospital corridor, lit by a single, flickering emergency light at the far end, creating deep shadows. A sense of immense emptiness. 16mm, low light.
Vertical shot: A close-up of a nurse's hand (not showing face) reaching towards a flickering light switch in a dark hospital room, extreme shallow depth of field, focus on the hand and switch.
Vertical shot: A narrow, tall window looking out onto heavy rain lashing down, obscuring everything outside. The glass is old and streaked.
Vertical shot: A fleeting, almost transparent silhouette of a figure in a white coat, just visible in the periphery of a dark hospital doorway, as if stepping out of view. Soft focus.
Vertical shot: A worn, chipped ceramic tea cup on a hospital desk, steam rising faintly, illuminated by a weak desk lamp. The background is a blurry dark corridor.

shorts.title: The Doctor's Touch in the Dark Ward
shorts.narration: The storm raged, plunging Jaffna Hospital's old wing into utter darkness. Only the feeble emergency lights fought the gloom. Nurse Amara stood over a critically ill child, her hands trembling as his breathing grew shallow. Then, that old, distinct antiseptic scent enveloped her. A terrifying cold, deeper than any draft, wrapped around her. She heard it: the soft, impossible clinking of metal instruments, right beside her. A faint, guiding pressure on her arm, steadying her trembling hands, almost physically guiding them. A soft, urgent whisper she couldn't understand. The child coughed, deeply. Just as panic surged, the power returned, flooding the ward with harsh light. The boy was stable, improving. On his clean sheet, a faint, precise circular mark. An unseen hand had been at work. The full story is on our channel.
visuals: Vertical shot: A nurse's silhouette hunched over a patient's bed in a dark ward, only the patient's form barely visible under a weak, yellow emergency light source from the floor. Intense shadow play.
Vertical shot: Close-up of a nurse's hand (not showing face) reaching for an oxygen mask in near darkness, fingers brushing against the fabric. The sense of urgency is palpable.
Vertical shot: A faint, shimmering outline of an old surgical tool, possibly a scalpel, half-visible against a dark, textured wall, catching a sliver of weak light. It appears to float.

Vertical shot: A pristine white hospital bed sheet, with a single, perfectly circular faint wet mark, like a ring from a glass or bottle, visible under harsh fluorescent light. The sheet is slightly rumpled.

Vertical shot: A long, narrow hospital corridor, the floor wet and reflective from a distant leak, reflecting the dim, flickering emergency lights into distorted patterns. No figures, just eerie emptiness.
